content:
After months of testing, macOS 27 Golden Gate is now rolling out to all users, bringing a brand-new Siri AI, deeper Liquid Glass refinements, major new Safari features, and a host of performance and usability improvements. Here's everything you need to know about this update.

At this year's WWDC, Apple took a slightly different approach to introducing its operating systems than users and developers have grown accustomed to.

Instead of going platform by platform, Apple spent less time on individual operating systems and focused more on cross-platform features and improvements—largely because many of these features rely on the new Apple Intelligence framework.

That said, macOS 27 Golden Gate still includes a number of thoughtful design and functional refinements, starting with several much-needed Liquid Glass adjustments.

Liquid Glass and Interface Improvements

While macOS Tahoe 26 adopted Apple's brand-new design language, it still lagged behind visually—especially compared to iOS 26 and iPadOS 26.

With macOS 27 Golden Gate, Apple has spent more time further integrating the new Liquid Glass throughout the system, while also bringing in some visual tweaks from iOS 27 and iPadOS 27—including a new Liquid Glass slider that lets users adjust the effect's transparency to their liking.

Hidden inside the Liquid Glass appearance settings is a fun little easter egg: Clarus the Dogcow—simply scroll the demo panel all the way to the bottom and you'll spot him.

macOS 27 Golden Gate also features redesigned app icons to better match the Liquid Glass design, adding depth and detail to Light, Dark, Tinted, and Clear global system appearances through additional layers.

The red, yellow, and green traffic light buttons introduced mid-beta have also been updated. The previously flat green, yellow, and red controls now sport a Liquid Glass look, with a delightful bounce effect when users click (or tap, briefly?) and drag before releasing.

Another thoughtful interface improvement in macOS 27 Golden Gate is Apple's decision to unify window and app corner radii across the entire system, rather than dynamically adjusting them based on UI elements in the window's menu bar.

While Apple's choice was deliberate, many people assumed the inconsistent corner radii were a bug—prompting Apple to specifically mention this change during the WWDC keynote.

Another controversial design decision involved icon counts. macOS 26 Tahoe added a symbol next to nearly every menu command, intending to make menus easier to scan—but it was widely criticized as making the interface more cluttered, and in some cases, harder to scan.

Fortunately, with macOS 27 Golden Gate, Apple has changed course, removing most of these icons and returning menus to a cleaner, more streamlined appearance.

Other visual refinements in macOS 27 Golden Gate include edge-to-edge sidebars and clearer distinction of the active window—both of which were controversial in macOS Tahoe 26.

Siri AI and the New Siri App

This is arguably the biggest new feature in macOS 27 Golden Gate. The new Siri, co-developed with Google's Gemini model, comes with its own dedicated app and is deeply integrated throughout the system.

The new Siri AI uses a new on-device indexing system to handle user data, and lives both in Spotlight and in the new Siri app.

The new Siri app looks and operates much like other AI assistant apps: a sidebar listing users' conversation history across compatible platforms, with a main chat panel in the center where you can type prompts, attach images or files, or start a conversation via voice. The app also supports searching and pinning conversations—a plus for users with different workflows.

The new Siri AI can draw information from the web and from users' personal information to provide practical, actionable answers. During beta, the new Siri received overwhelmingly positive feedback, although it can sometimes be a bit slower than users accustomed to other LLM-powered AI assistants might expect.

Another practical feature of the new Siri AI is its ability to interact with both native and third-party apps and perform actions directly—dramatically improving on the old Siri's app integration capabilities.

Developers need to expose their apps' content and functionality through the App Intents framework, so as more developers update their apps for macOS 27 Golden Gate, this area is expected to continue improving.

Finally, the system adds a universal "Ask Siri" right-click menu option, letting users select text, images, or files and query Siri directly. For example, you can Control-click on an image in a document and ask Siri for more information, or select a passage of text and ask Siri to rewrite, proofread, adjust the tone, or offer writing suggestions.

Siri AI supports English at launch, with French, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese, and Spanish joining in October. Due to regulatory reasons, Siri AI is temporarily unavailable in China and the EU.

Apple Intelligence

We've covered Apple's new foundation models in detail before, but in short, with its 2027 OS releases, Apple has developed a new generation of Apple Intelligence models. Here's Apple's official description of each:

AFM 3 Core, the next generation of our 3-billion-parameter dense model, with further quality improvements. AFM 3 Core Advanced, our most powerful on-device model, with native multimodal support, and support for more expressive voice and higher-accuracy dictation. This 20-billion-parameter model is built on Apple's most cutting-edge research and uses a sparse architecture, activating only 1 to 4 billion parameters as needed. AFM 3 Core Advanced requires and is optimized for our most powerful Apple Silicon systems. AFM 3 Cloud, our server-side workhorse model, designed for speed, efficiency, and capability. ADM 3 Cloud (Image), for image generation and editing, unlocking more advanced photo editing tools, a new Image Playground, and more. AFM 3 Cloud Pro, our most powerful server-side model, powering the most demanding use cases such as agentic tool use and complex reasoning.

In practice, macOS 27 Golden Gate uses two on-device models—AFM 3 Core and AFM 3 Core Advanced—with the rest running in the cloud. The performance of these two on-device models depends on the Mac's hardware, particularly available memory, to handle their activated parameters and other AI workloads.

As for Apple Intelligence's real-world performance in macOS 27 Golden Gate, it's a mixed bag. The models themselves perform quite well on everyday tasks—such as helping draft emails, proofreading documents, or summarizing content.

The problem is that Apple now sometimes seems overly enthusiastic about how and when Siri AI is presented—sometimes making users feel annoyed, or even getting in the way of what they're trying to accomplish.

One standout new Apple Intelligence feature in macOS 27 Golden Gate is the new Visual Intelligence shortcut. Simply press Command-Shift-Space and you can select any area of the screen to instantly query Siri—be it an image, PDF, text, or almost anything displayed on screen.

Unfortunately, not all Macs compatible with macOS 27 will be able to run the new Apple Intelligence—the feature requires an A18 Pro, M1, or later chip. Here's the official list of Mac models Apple says support the new features:

  • MacBook Neo (2026)
  • MacBook Air with Apple Silicon (2020 or later)
  • MacBook Pro with Apple Silicon (2020 or later)
  • iMac with Apple Silicon (2021 or later)
  • Mac mini with Apple Silicon (2020 or later)
  • Mac Studio (2022 or later)
  • Mac Pro with Apple Silicon (2023)

Most Apple Intelligence features support the languages already available for Apple Intelligence, including Simplified Chinese, Traditional Chinese, Danish, Dutch, English, French, German, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Norwegian, Portuguese, Spanish, Swedish, Turkish, and Vietnamese.

Due to regulatory reasons, Apple Intelligence is temporarily unavailable in China. Apple has also noted that some Apple Intelligence and Siri AI features will have usage restrictions, though the company has not yet released specifics.

Performance and Stability Improvements

During the WWDC26 keynote, Apple highlighted dozens of improvements that apply across all operating systems.

For macOS 27 Golden Gate, these include faster AirDrop transfers, improved network file browsing, faster Spotlight indexing (especially for shortcuts and actions), and faster iCloud Photos uploads with selective priority syncing.

macOS 27 Golden Gate also improves scrolling performance in Safari and Calendar, as well as animation performance in Mission Control and Spaces. Apple has also tweaked Mail indexing and search, and the underlying system for Spotlight suggestions.

Other improvements include more consistent and persistent window position memory across external displays, HDR support for system UI elements, broader support for high-resolution and high-refresh-rate modes on external displays, and more complete Sidecar touch support—including tap controls, single-finger scrolling, system gestures, and markup features.

Safari

macOS 27 Golden Gate introduces a new Safari feature called "Notify Me" that can monitor web pages and alert users when relevant changes occur—such as price drops, restocks, event registration openings, or just about anything users want to track.

"Notify Me" can check hourly, daily, weekly, or monthly, and can additionally specify the days and times to check.

Additionally, Safari in macOS 27 Golden Gate adds "Describe an Extension," letting users create extensions using natural language.

To help users get started, Apple provides several examples covering productivity, focus, creativity, and design development. Users can also simply describe what they need in their own words and let Apple Intelligence handle the rest.

Both features can be accessed from the "More Options" hamburger menu on the right side of the current tab.

For users who like to have tons of tabs open throughout the day, Safari can now automatically organize and group tabs by topic.

Another nice touch in Safari for macOS 27 Golden Gate is the new pull-to-refresh gesture, similar to iOS and iPadOS, where users can swipe down past the "rubber band" effect to refresh the page.

This gesture also works in other system apps like Mail, News, and Calendar; many see this as a further hint at the rumored touch-screen Mac, which could be announced as early as this year.

iPhone Mirroring

With macOS 27 Golden Gate, users can now resize the iPhone Mirroring window to different aspect ratios; many see this as an early sign that Apple is paving the way for a foldable iPhone.

Now that iPhone Duo is officially out, Mac users can get an early taste of the experience. Unfortunately, Apple notes that iPhone Mirroring is still unavailable in the EU.

Shortcuts

This is arguably one of the most practical new Apple Intelligence features in this year's OS updates.

While Shortcuts itself is a fairly approachable automation tool, it can still feel intimidating to everyday users. Now, users simply need to describe what they want to accomplish, and Apple Intelligence will build it into a native shortcut.

To help users get started, the Shortcuts app also highlights several suggestions on the new shortcut creation screen, including:

  • Dictate and translate to Spanish
  • Write a haiku for the weather forecast
  • Play my workout playlist when I arrive at the gym
  • Build a recipe from these leftovers
  • Summarize my day each morning
  • Prioritize my to-do list each morning
  • Get driving directions as soon as I get in the car
  • Dictate my thoughts and save them to the clipboard
  • Dim the screen when bedtime starts
  • Turn on Do Not Disturb when opening the TV app

By the way, if you want to dive deeper into Shortcuts, be sure to follow Stephen Robles on YouTube and Instagram. You can also check out MacStories' Shortcuts Playground, a more powerful natural language shortcut builder.

Photos

The Photos app now offers three editing tools powered by Apple Intelligence: an enhanced "Clean Up" tool that can remove objects, people, or other unwanted elements from photos; "Extend," which can generate surrounding areas when you feel the original crop was too tight; and "Spatial Recompose," which lets you change the angle and composition of a photo after it's been taken.

Additionally, iCloud Shared Albums now supports full-resolution sharing and can invite Windows and Android users to join via iCloud.com.

Other new features include the ability to play any set of photos and videos as a slideshow with custom music, transitions, and playback duration, a photo rating feature with a new star rating system, and a brand-new dedicated "Shot by Me" collection.

More macOS 27 Golden Gate Details

  • Calendar lets users add, edit, or update events by describing them.
  • Finder can now intelligently suggest names based on the contents of files and folders.
  • Image Playground has expanded its support for different styles and uses a new foundation model for better results.
  • Maps' Flyover experience has been enhanced, with improved textures, detail, and clarity for hundreds of cities worldwide.
  • Messages has finally (finally) integrated tapback notifications and improved cross-device sync performance.
  • Notes supports handwriting and drawing with the trackpad, expanded Markdown support, and adds copy/paste and Section Links functionality.
  • Podcasts now supports video podcasts with picture-in-picture playback.

macOS 27 Golden Gate also marks the last version to support Rosetta. As Apple explains, "only apps that have not been updated after installing this update will be unable to run on Macs with Apple Silicon"—you can learn more here.

Compatibility

According to Apple's official list, macOS 27 Golden Gate is compatible with the following Mac models:

  • MacBook Neo (2026)

What's your favorite new feature? Let us know in the comments.
